sources.design: taxonomic review of far-transfer literature
sources.finding_quote: Despite a century's worth of research, arguments surrounding the question of whether far transfer occurs have made little progress toward resolution. ... Estimation of a single effect size for far transfer is misguided in view of this complexity. The past 100 years of research shows that evidence for transfer under some conditions is substantial, but critical conditions for many key questions are untested.

sources.design: 3 meta-analyses: chess, music, and working-memory training vs cognitive/academic transfer
sources.finding_quote: The results show small to moderate effects. However, the effect sizes are inversely related to the quality of the experimental design (e.g., presence of active control groups). ... far transfer of learning rarely occurs.

sources.design: review + meta-analysis of environmental context-dependent memory studies
sources.finding_quote: The meta-analysis showed that across all studies, environmental context effects were reliable, and furthermore, that the use of noncontextual cues during learning (overshadowing) and at test (outshining), as well as mental reinstatement of appropriate context cues at test, all reduce the effect of environmental manipulations.

sources.design: meta-analysis of contextual interference (randomized vs blocked practice), 61 studies
sources.finding_quote: A meta-analysis of the contextual interference effect produced 139 estimates of effect sizes from 61 studies. The average overall effect size was .38. The effect size for basic research (.57) was significantly different from applied research (.19).

replication.result: failed (for far transfer under rigorous designs)

backfire.condition: high contextual interference (practice conditions varied, not matched to the target) improves retention/transfer relative to blocked matched practice — tension with 'make practice resemble the target'
context-dependent effects shrink or vanish once encoding/retrieval encourage non-contextual (introspective) processing

sources.finding_quote: Concreteness training resulted in significantly greater decreases in depressive symptoms and significantly greater increases in concrete thinking than the waiting-list and the bogus training control, and significantly greater decreases in rumination than the waiting-list control.

sources.design: review of constructive vs unconstructive repetitive thought
sources.finding_quote: The main unconstructive consequences of RT are (a) depression, (b) anxiety, and (c) difficulties in physical health. ... the level of construal (abstract vs. concrete processing) adopted during RT [is a key principle].

replication.result: mixed (package-level effect; no isolation of the chain-analysis component)

backfire.condition: abstract, evaluative repetitive thought (rumination) is the unconstructive pole; concrete reconstruction must stay concrete or it risks sliding into abstract rumination

sources.design: review reframing planning fallacy as memory bias for past durations

sources.design: 3 experiments supplying feedback on actual past task duration before a new prediction
sources.finding_quote: In all 3 experiments, supplying feedback increased predictive accuracy. Overall, results indicate that, when predicting duration, people do well when they rely not on memory of past task duration but instead on measures of actual duration, whether their own or that of others.

sources.design: meta-analytic review of adult CBT outcome across anxiety disorders, 108 trials
sources.finding_quote: Cognitive therapy and exposure therapy alone, in combination, or combined with relaxation training, were efficacious across the anxiety disorders, with no differential efficacy for any treatment components for any specific diagnoses.

sources.design: meta-analysis + meta-regression of self-help treatment for anxiety disorders, 56 articles/82 comparisons
sources.effect: g=0.78 vs waitlist/placebo; g=-0.20 vs face-to-face
sources.finding_quote: When self-help treatment was compared to wait-list or placebo, a meta-analysis indicated a moderate to large effect size (g=0.78). When self-help treatment was compared to face-to-face treatment, results indicated a small effect that favored the latter (g=-0.20).

replication.result: replicated (self-help effective vs control across 56 studies, smaller than face-to-face)

backfire.condition: self-guided delivery reliably underperforms therapist-guided delivery (g=-0.20), bounding the 'adjacent' transfer claim

sources.design: conceptual and evidence review of choice bracketing
sources.finding_quote: When making many choices, a person can broadly bracket them by assessing the consequences of all of them taken together, or narrowly bracket them by making each choice in isolation.

sources.finding_quote: Smokers increased their preference for LL rewards when 'bundling' of individual decisions into a sequence was either suggested or forced. This preference increased with repeated experience. Non-smokers showed neither pattern.

sources.design: combined vs separated snack-choice experiments; diversification bias
sources.effect: combined choice increases variety-seeking beyond revealed preference
sources.finding_quote: There appears to be at least one situation in which combined choices actually leave consumers worse off. ... [subjects] showed much more variety seeking when making simultaneous choices (64% chose three different items) than when making sequential choices (9%).

backfire.condition: diversification bias: broad/combined bracketing of repeated same-kind choices produces more variety-seeking than people's own separated choices reveal they want, leaving them worse off

sources.design: 4 studies on perceived goal progress and licensing of inconsistent choices
